messages.author: 8d7e6559e413a92b
messages.subject: INLA model crashing
parts:
Hi All, 

I'm experiencing some strange behavior after updating INLA. 

Prior to the update, I was running large models (>600k observations) with multiple i.i.d. random effects, including one with ~3000 units. 

To speed things up, I was using EB integration and Gaussian approximation. On my machine with 36GB ram, this was working fine. 

However, because I wanted to experiment with Pardiso and adaptive integration, I updated my version of INLA and setup a Pardiso license. 

For the new models, I used auto integration, adaptive proximation, and I set config=T, because I want to sample from the posterior. 

However, now, when I run a large model e.g.( >600k observations), my model crashes. At first, I assumed this was a problem caused by one of the new settings + the size of my data. However, I kept reducing the complexity of the model and finally started working with a simple regression model, which I show below. 

Across models, once I exceed a few hundred thousand observations, the model starts crashing. 

I've included my output in txt file and the code used to simulate the data and run the model (at the end of this msg). I'm estimating this model using what I understand to be the cheapest estimation strategy and the model itself is trivial. Given that I've estimated much more complex models with around 800k observations, I know that this is not a hardware capacity problem (or it least, it wasn't a few days ago). 

I have tried reinstalling both the stable and dev versions of INLA. I have also restarted R and not specified my Pardiso license, which I assumed would force reliance on the default computational approach. 

I have also restarted my machine and immediately run the model on the simulated data. The model still crashed. 

Any insight into what might be causing this and/or how to fix it would be hugely appreciated. 

Thanks!

Best,
Joe




N = 700000
x = rnorm(N, 0, 1)
y = 1 + .5*x + rnorm(N, 0, .8)
d = data.frame(y=y,x=x)
 
ff <- y ~ x                                                                                                                                                  
p <- list(mean.intercept = 0, 
                   prec.intercept = .001, 
                   mean = list( x = 0),
                   prec = list( x = .01))

mrp.iid.m <- inla(ff,  data=d,
                  #Specify priors for fixed effects
                  control.fixed=p,
                  control.inla=list(int.strategy='eb', 
                                    strategy='gaussian'),
                  control.predictor = list(compute=T),
                  control.compute = list(config=F), 
                  verbose=T)

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA model crashing
parts:
On Mon, 2018-09-17 at 15:08 -0700, Joseph Hoover wrote:
> For the new models, I used auto integration, adaptive proximation,
> and I set config=T, because I want to sample from the posterior.
>
> However, now, when I run a large model e.g.( >600k observations), my
> model crashes.

Hi. this is weird.

if you set up pardiso with license, you can always revert back to the
'old'/default setting using

control.compute = list(smtp="taucs")

the taucs library is still there, just that there is an additional
option via pardiso.


with you model, which in the example is 'long and thin', sometimes
'taucs' crash due to an internal (taucs-) error when nested dissection
is used for the reordering. in this cases it can be rescued using

control.inla = list(reordering = "amdc")

for example (or anything but 'metis', or 'auto'). can you check if this
helps?

Best
H

messages.author: 8d7e6559e413a92b
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA model crashing
parts:
Hello Professor Rue, 

Thank you for your advice. I went to implement it this morning; however, I very oddly found that I was able to fit the above model to the simulated data on one of my machines. However, on another machine (my primary machine, one that I've previously fit large INLA models on, and one that has comparable specs) even after following your suggestions, I'm observing the same behavior.  

On a slightly different note, since things seem to be working for now on one of my machines, I fit my target model (using gaussian and eb). Using the fitted object, I wanted to test the code I've developed for batch prediction based on inla.posterior.sample. Unfortunately, inla.posterior.sample throws a segmentation fault and provides no additional information on what's causing the crash. 

While running inla.posterior.sample, I'm using only 10% of my available RAM and approximately one core. I wound up digging into the function code a little bit and noticed that inla.qsample takes a reordering argument. Per your suggestion above, I thought that perhaps specifying reordering as 'amdc' would solve the problem. However, it did not. 

Again, when I fit a model with a smaller amount of data, I am able to run posterior.sample without any issues. 

Thank you for your help!

Best,
Joe

messages.author: 8d7e6559e413a92b
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA model crashing
parts:
Hi Again, 

I just found that on both machines, I can estimate the simple linear regression with N=700k if and only if I use Pardiso. It appears that Taucs crashes, regardless of whether I specify a different reordering algorithm. I feel like this conflicts with my observations yesterday, as I thought that I was initially using Pardiso. However, regardless, that is what I am now observing. 

Also, I should note that I can fit the simple regression model with 300k observations in ~50 seconds. However, fitting the model with 700k observations takes ~50 minutes. I understand that the relationship between computational time and N is not necessarily a linear function, but should an increase of this magnitude be expected in such a simple model?

Thank you!

Best,
Joe

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA model crashing
parts:
Hello, 

Thank you, I will try this. 

However, do you have any insight into why inla.posterior.sample() would be crashing? Given that I am only able to estimate large models with Pardiso, I am wondering if inla.qsample's apparent reliance on Taucs might be the root of the problem (though, maybe I'm wrong about qsample relying on Taucs?). If this is the case, is there anyway to specify that Pardiso is used for posterior sampling?

Of course, the problem may be something else entirely, but I am not sure whether it is something that can be corrected or how to isolate it, at this point. 

Thank you!

Best,
Joe

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA model crashing
parts:
good point. this issue was lacking a little behind and usage was really
counterintuitive. you should be able to do

inla.setOption(smtp="pardiso") ## needed for posterior.sample, qinv()
## and qsample()
r = inla(..., control.compute = list(
openmp.strategy = "pardiso.serial")) ## or pardiso.parallel

## must set number of threads here (currently...)
x = inla.posterior.sample(100, r, num.threads = 12)

with the new testing-version 18.09.18

All this stuff with how pardiso is spesified is a little experimental
for the moment, and it might be /will be, some changes later on....


H
